I farm only 3.0 mu, and I am 74 years old, so I will keep my plan practical, familiar, and low-risk. I have grown wheat and maize for many years, and with a wheat-maize rotation on irrigated land, I will stay with the cropping pattern I know best. I will use better seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want stable emergence, better stress tolerance, and dependable yield from a small area. I will not push fertilizer to extremes; I will apply enough nitrogen for yield, with moderate phosphorus and potassium to keep the soil productive and support grain filling. Because I have access to well irrigation, I will irrigate wheat more times than maize, since wheat in my area depends more on timely water at key stages, while summer maize can use rainfall plus a small number of well irrigations if needed. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage on a small farm and fits my usual practice. I will also keep pesticide applications limited to what is needed to control the main diseases, insects, and weeds, because I want to protect yield without making the work too heavy. My goal this year is steady production and manageable fieldwork rather than taking extra risk.
